regions.text: freedom— symbolizing an end as well as a beginning— signifying
regions.explanation: From 4.70s to 7.22s (“freedom— symbolizing an end as well as a beginning— …”), 2 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 375 ms to 0 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.

metrics.name: pause_length
metrics.threshold: >= 0.3 s longer than reference, mid-phrase (no punctuation)

regions.explanation: At 13.04s, between “oath” and “our”, a 970 ms silence replaced the reference's 140 ms pause. A long silence where the reference has none - especially mid-phrase - breaks the syntactic unit and signals lost place rather than deliberate emphasis. Fix: Keep this phrase in one breath; pause at the punctuation instead.

From 19.07s to 20.52s (“world is very different now.”), articulation rate slowed to 5.52 syll/s against 7.21 syll/s in the reference (-23%); that is 1.5× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.
